[1.0] THE STATELESS PARADIGM & ZERO-STORAGE INVARIANCE

Conventional URL shorteners (e.g. bit.ly, tinyurl.com, t.co) operate as stateful centralized key-value brokers. When a link is shortened, the server generates a random 6-to-8 character key, writes an entry into an SQL or Redis database (id -> long_url), and returns the key.

This architecture creates profound vulnerabilities: links break when services shut down (“link rot”), servers incur ongoing hosting costs, centralized operators can track and profile click activity, and single database outages take down millions of redirects simultaneously.

unpu.re replaces stateful storage with pure information theory. The short code is not an ID or pointer; it is the fully serialized, entropy-compressed payload of the destination URL itself. The compression function f(url) -> token and decompression function f⁻¹(token) -> url are purely mathematical and deterministic. Zero bytes of database storage exist, meaning links never expire and can be decoded offline indefinitely.

[2.0] BITSTREAM ENTROPY FRAMING & MULTI-TIER DICTIONARY CODEC

General-purpose compression algorithms (gzip, brotli, zstd) fail on short strings (30–80 bytes) because their framing headers, checksums, and dynamic Huffman trees produce 40–70 bytes of overhead, often resulting in negative compression.

unpu.re bypasses byte boundaries using a custom fractional bitstream compiler. Bits are packed sequentially with zero alignment padding:

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | UNPU.RE V2.1 BITSTREAM PACKET LAYOUT | +---------+-----------------+-----------------------+------------------------------------------------+ | MODE | SCHEME (2 bits) | HOST ROUTING (1 - 20b)| MULTI-TIER TOKEN STREAM (4b - 18b per element) | | (1 bit) | 00: https://www | 0: 65k Dict Domain | T0: High-freq delimiters & routes (6 bits) | | 0: Comp | 01: http://www | 10: Platform Subdomain| T1: Common web tokens, TLDs, query (10 bits) | | 1: Id | 10: https:// | 11: Custom Hostname | T2: 10k Vocab (Lower/Title/Upper + CamelCase) | | | 11: http:// | | T3: Nibble-Packed Hex Mode (4 bits/char) | | | | | T4: Decimal BCD Digit Mode (4 bits/digit) | | | | | T5: Literal ASCII Byte Fallback (14 bits) | +---------+-----------------+-----------------------+------------------------------------------------+
  • Mode Bit (1 bit): Bit 0 indicates the compressed multi-tier bitstream. If an uncompressible payload is detected where compressed bits exceed raw 8-bit octets, the encoder automatically invokes Mode 1 (Identity Escape Floor), guaranteeing zero expansion.
  • Scheme Framing Header (2 bits): Encodes the URL protocol:
    00 = https://www. | 01 = http://www. | 10 = https:// | 11 = http://
  • Host Routing (Top 65k Domains & Platform Subdomains):
    • 00 + 16-bit unsigned integer: Domain matches top 65,536 Tranco telemetry index, followed by trailing path tokens.
    • 01 + 16-bit unsigned integer: Domain matches dictionary, terminating bare domain (e.g. https://google.com collapses into 2 bits + 2 bits + 16 bits = 20 bits \(pprox\) 4 Base64 characters).
    • 10 + 4-bit Platform ID: Multi-tenant developer/blog platforms (github.io, wordpress.com, substack.com, medium.com, pages.dev, vercel.app, etc.), followed by subdomain tokens.
    • 11 + host tokens: Generic custom domain fallback.
  • Path Token Stream (Multi-Tier Entropy Hierarchy):
    • Tier 0 (6 bits): Prefix 0 + 5-bit index (32 high-frequency routes, connectives, and query separators such as /blog/, /api/v1/, -to-, &id=, /, -). Slot 31 is the End-of-Stream (EOS) delimiter.
    • Tier 1 (10 bits): Prefix 10 + 8-bit index (256 common web tokens, modern TLDs like .io, .ai, news article calendar date tokens /01/–/12/, and query parameters like searchResultPosition=).
    • Tier 2 (18 bits): 10,000 frequency-ranked English words and high-profile global news entities (trump, biden, greenland, etc.). Supports CamelCase Segmentation (e.g. searchResultPosition → search + Result + Position) and Compound Subword Splitting.
    • Tier 3 (Nibble-Packed Hex Mode - 4 bits/char): Prefix 11110 + 6-bit length + 1-bit case. Packs 2 hexadecimal characters per byte into 4-bit nibbles.
    • Tier 4 (Decimal BCD Digit Mode - 4 bits/digit): Prefix 111110 + 6-bit length. Packs continuous decimal digits (dates, timestamps, IDs) into 4-bit Binary Coded Decimal.
    • Tier 5 (14 bits): Prefix 111111 + 8-bit literal ASCII byte fallback for unindexed characters.
  • Radix-64 URL-Safe Serialization: The variable bitstream is packed into 8-bit octets and serialized using RFC 4648 URL-safe Base64 ([A-Za-z0-9_-]), omitting trailing = padding characters for clean, typeable paths.
[3.0] GITHUB PAGES ZERO-SERVER 404 ROUTING LIFECYCLE

GitHub Pages is an immutable static CDN without server-side rewrite capabilities (no try_files, PHP, or Cloudflare Workers). Under normal operations, navigating to a non-existent path returns a 404 status.

unpu.re turns this limitation into a client-side routing bus:

[CLIENT] ---> HTTP GET https://unpu.re/hKTAqfQqB8A | [GITHUB PAGES CDN] | +-----------+-----------+ | Path exists on disk? | | NO (Dynamic token) | +-----------------------+ | Serves repo custom /404.html (HTTP 404) | [BROWSER PARSING] | Synchronous <head> script executes BEFORE layout or DOM render | extractCode() reads window.location.pathname -> "hKTAqfQqB8A" | decodeUrl() decompresses bitstream in CPU registers (< 0.01 ms) | window.location.replace("https://example.com/blog/lorem-ipsum") | [INSTANT CLIENT REDIRECTION]
  • Pre-Render Head Execution: The decompression decoder runs synchronously inside the <head> before any stylesheet parsing, image fetching, or DOM tree rendering occurs. Redirection takes place in under 5 milliseconds.
  • History Preservation: Calling window.location.replace() rather than window.location.href overwrites the 404 entry in the browser session history. Pressing the “Back” button returns the user cleanly to their previous page without trapping them in a redirect loop.
  • Dual Routing Topology: The system supports both clean paths (https://unpu.re/<code> via 404.html) and fragment identifiers (https://unpu.re/#<code> via index.html) seamlessly.
[4.0] DECOMPRESSION BENCHMARKS & COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS

Because the 65,536-domain array and 10,000-word vocabulary are pre-sorted lexicographically, domain resolution operates in \(O(\log_2 N)\) time, word lookup in \(O(1)\) time, and bitstream deserialization in linear \(O(L)\) time with respect to the short code length:
